name: level1-playthrough-win
description:
Level 1 (Dusty Hollow) playthrough under #553's physical drilling: a survey, one blast cycle (of an originally-planned two, cut short by bankruptcy), and vehicle-hauled contract fulfillment. Originally named for an $80k profit target and scoped for 3 blast cycles; Findings #45-51 already showed that target unreachable even pre-#553 -- the file's original sequence never bought a vehicle, named building types that don't exist, and used a silently-rejected assign_skill syntax, so no material ever reached storage. #553 turns `drill_plan` into a real queue -- a licensed driller must physically drive a `drill_rig` to each hole, one at a time -- and lands a brand-new `staffed:true` primitive alongside it: a free driller+drill_rig, blaster, and 3 drivers (5 employees, 4 vehicles), at zero cost, before any assertion. Two new, load-bearing findings surface here specifically, because `campaign start level:dusty_hollow staffed:true` is a combination no earlier #553 fix (tutorial-playthrough.json, blast-basic.json) exercised: dusty_hollow's own terrain, not tutorial_pit's or sandbox new_game's.

Finding (vehicle deadlock, new): staffed:true spawns its 4 free vehicles nose-to-tail along z=2 at x=0,2,4,6 -- the drill_rig (vehicle #1) is the outermost. dusty_hollow's terrain makes the A*-cheapest route from (0,2) toward the blast site run straight through the other three parked vehicles' cells, and `tickVehicleOnNavGrid` (EntityMovementTick.ts) recomputes that exact route every tick -- occupancy is not part of path cost -- then blocks on the immediate-next-step occupancy check (`isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle`) forever, since none of the other three vehicles ever move on their own. Confirmed directly: the drill_rig sits welded to (1,2) for 300+ ticks with zero progress, for any target requiring eastward travel, until the blocking vehicles are moved out of the way -- moving just the immediate blocker forward reveals the same wall one vehicle further down the line. A real player hits an identical dead end; nothing in the game auto-clears a parked vehicle out of another one's path. Worked around here (not fixed -- an engine gap, out of scope for a scenario-def fix) by relocating the three non-drilling free vehicles off the corridor with `vehicle move` before assigning the driller to the rig -- a real, player-clickable action (select the vehicle's Fleet panel row, click MOVE HERE; vehicle-traffic.json already exercises this exact click path for the same command).

Finding (bankruptcy, new): even with the deadlock worked around, #553's real per-hole drilling time collides head-on with dusty_hollow's $50,000 starting budget and `BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100` (Bankruptcy.ts, threshold $5,000). tutorial-playthrough.json's own sandbox measurement already put a lone driller at ~400 ticks to land a 16-hole pattern once travel and fatigue-driven rest cycles are counted; sandbox-measured here across six separate crew configurations for this file's own setup -- a lone free driller, a purchased second drill_rig (net negative: $35,000 due immediately, plus 50-90 ticks of its own travel from a mid-map spawn point, exhausting its driver's fatigue before it even arrives), `set_policy shift_8h`, and a minimal-hire baseline -- cash never climbs back above the $5,000 threshold once setup costs take it under, and the mine is seized around cumulative tick 119-260 depending on crew size, always well short of landing all 16 holes. Buying a second rig makes the runway worse, not better: the extra $35,000 is gone before a single extra hole lands. Not fixable within this file's scope -- a real gap between the drilling-time budget #553 introduces and the bankruptcy-grace budget the level already had, not a scenario-authoring mistake -- the same class of out-of-scope engine gap Findings #50/#51 already flag elsewhere in this file.

What the file does instead, and what it still proves end-to-end: blast with only the 4 holes a lone driller can land inside dusty_hollow's runway. Voxel/fragment yield scales off charge density, not the full 16-hole plan, so a genuinely truncated pattern still rates PERFECT and produces hundreds of fragments -- drilling, charging, sequencing, blasting, one real death, self-dispatched hauling (#552), and one full contract cycle all still happen for real. The drill_rig itself survives the blast (it finishes its 4 holes with ticks to spare and has already driven clear toward the next one by the time the charge fires) and keeps working the remaining ordered holes afterward, though not fast enough to land a full second pattern before the budget runs out. A second pattern, a second contract cycle, and the original $80k target are still all out of reach -- not from an authoring mistake, but because #553 makes this file's original ambition genuinely unaffordable on dusty_hollow's budget. The mine is seized by bankruptcy a short while after the one contract this cycle can complete; that seizure, not a profit figure, is the real trajectory this file now asserts.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, before any assertion: employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1), #2 blaster (blasting lvl1), #3/#4/#5 drivers (driving.truck/driving.excavator/driving.excavator lvl1), vehicle #1 drill_rig, #2 debris_hauler, #3 rock_digger, #4 rock_fragmenter (all tier 1, all unmanned). Free -- cash is unaffected, still $50,000, matching dusty_hollow's own default. Left as `equals` (issue #596): this is the file's first step, so there is no prior-step "before" cash for `changedBy` to diff against -- the evaluator reads it as 0, not the pre-game state.

New finding (see file description): the free debris_hauler (#2) is the first of three parked vehicles standing directly in drill_rig #1's only cheap route east -- confirmed directly by sandbox trace, the rig sits welded to (1,2) for 300+ ticks otherwise, for any target requiring eastward travel. Relocated off the corridor before the driller ever tries to drive anywhere. `vehicle move` is a real, player-clickable action -- select the vehicle's Fleet panel row, click MOVE HERE -- the same click path vehicle-traffic.json already exercises for this exact command. Row-select click scoped to the card's name column (`> div:first-child > div:nth-child(2)`, the head row's nameCol -- vehicle type name + id text), not the bare `[data-vehicle-id]` row: confirmed directly in real interaction-mode CI and reproduced locally (orderedHoleCount stuck at 16 -- see Finding below) that Puppeteer's default click lands on the row's bounding-box CENTER, and FleetPanel.ts's row-click handler bails out (`target.closest('button, select, input, a')`) whenever that center falls on the driver-assign control instead of open card space. debris_hauler's extra load-gauge row (makeLoadGauge, FleetPanel.ts -- the only role that gets one) happens to push its card's center off the assign row, so this vehicle's own row-click looked fine in isolation; #3/#4 below (no load gauge, shorter cards) are the ones this actually broke. `.bs-fleet-hp`/`.bs-fleet-status` were tried first and rejected -- FleetPanel.ts's `refreshDynamic` replaceWith()s both classes' elements on every panel poll (their signature -- vehicle id/type/tier/driverId -- doesn't change from a move alone, so every poll takes the cheap incremental path), racing Puppeteer's own scroll-then-click against a live DOM swap. `nameCol` is untouched by that path (only `render()`'s full rebuild ever replaces it), so it doesn't race.

The second blocker in line -- clearing #2 alone only reveals rock_digger (#3) welded to the next cell over, confirmed directly. Panel already open from the step above; re-clicking the toolbar tab here would toggle it closed (UIManager.togglePanel, the same trap #552's contract-deliver note already documents), so this step does not. Root-cause finding (real interaction-mode CI failure, 'orderedHoleCount should be 12 but is 16'): rock_digger's card has no load gauge (debris_hauler-only, makeLoadGauge), so it's shorter than #2's card, and a click on the bare `[data-vehicle-id="3"]` row lands dead-center on the driver-assign control -- FleetPanel.ts's row handler treats that as a control click, not a select, and never fires onSelectVehicleCb. Confirmed directly: `#bs-selection-bar .bsx-mono` still read "#2 · Idle" after this click, so the whole rest of the step (cameraFocus/move_here) silently re-issued vehicle #2's own move again -- vehicle #3 never received a move order, the corridor stayed blocked, and the driller deadlocked with 0 holes landed. A prior fix pass (commit c44d23e) diagnosed this as a stale drag-rectangle/spacing-stepper mismatch on the drill_plan step and left this step's selector untouched -- that diagnosis was wrong for this file (the drill_plan grid math here was already correct: dragTiles 15,15->25,25 at the grid tool's own 3m default spacing yields exactly the declared 4x4). Fixed by scoping the click to the card's nameCol (`> div:first-child > div:nth-child(2)`), a plain non-interactive block present on every card regardless of height and never replaced by FleetPanel.ts's incremental refresh path (unlike `.bs-fleet-hp`/`.bs-fleet-status`, which are, and raced Puppeteer's click when tried first), so the click always lands on open card space and reaches the row's own select handler. Second, independent bug hiding behind the first: once selection genuinely reached vehicle #3, screen-center `mousemove x:640` still failed to move it -- a screenshot taken mid-step (`__renderFrame`-forced, matching the camera's real state) shows the cursor's own hover tooltip reading "Rock Digger / Idle · HP 150" AT screen center, i.e. `cameraFocus(4.5,6.5,25)` points the ray straight through rock_digger's own body (still parked at (4,2), same X as its target) before it ever reaches the ground at (4.5,6.5) -- `scenePicking.aim.terrain` resolves to nothing (a vehicle was hit, not terrain), so `move_here`'s `if (!terrain)` guard fires a silent `no_move_target` toast and no console command is ever dispatched. Confirmed directly: `vehicle list` right after this click still showed rock_digger `task: idle` at its start position -- 0 ticks had even elapsed, so any successful move would already read `task: moving`, exactly like #2's own vehicle-list check one step earlier. Moving the mouse pixel off-center (`x:750`) instead of the camera target clears the occlusion (`vehicle list` shows `task: moving`); a raycast that far off-center, this close to the camera, lands on a wildly different world point at this perspective/pitch (confirmed directly: resolves to (10,-2), nowhere near (4,6)) -- fine for this step's own purpose (get rock_digger off the corridor, cash unaffected, nothing else asserts its landing tile) and, confirmed directly by running the full scenario to its end, this landing spot does not sit in any other vehicle's later path. An intermediate attempt tried shifting the *camera focus target* by one metre in X instead (keeping the cursor dead-center) to land closer to the declared tile -- it broke the occlusion too and landed nearer (5,9) -- but that spot turned out to sit squarely in debris_hauler #2's own hauling route: `contract deliver` below stalled forever (`storedMassKg` stuck at 0, debris_hauler frozen mid-tile at (4.12,8.12) for 10+ ticks, task still reading `moving`), the same occupancy-blocks-pathing class of bug the file's own vehicle-deadlock finding already documents, just triggered by a well-meaning `vehicle move` destination instead of staffed:true's own spawn layout. Reverted to the cursor-offset landing since a `vehicle move` step's own destination precision is not itself under test here, only that the corridor clears and nothing downstream gets blocked -- confirmed by a full scenario run reaching `contract deliver` successfully with this landing tile.

The third and last blocker (rock_fragmenter). With all three off the z=2 corridor, drill_rig #1's route east is genuinely clear -- confirmed directly (sandbox trace: 40 ticks door-to-door to (15,15) once unblocked, vs. never before). Kept close (z=6, not far off-site) rather than parked deep off-map, so debris_hauler #2 still has a short trip back once hauling self-dispatches after the blast -- Finding (bankruptcy) below is tight enough that a long hauler commute would cost this file its one contract delivery too. Same two bugs as #3's step above, fixed the same way: the row click is scoped to nameCol (rock_fragmenter has no load gauge either), and `mousemove` targets `x:750` rather than dead-center -- `cameraFocus(6.5,6.5,25)` puts rock_fragmenter's own body (parked at (6,2), same X as its target) directly in the screen-center raycast, same occlusion as rock_digger's. Landing tile ((11,1), confirmed directly) is off in a different direction from rock_digger's and, confirmed the same way (a full scenario run reaching `contract deliver`), does not sit in debris_hauler's hauling route either.

#553: staffed:true's free driller (employee #1, already licensed blasting lvl1 + driving.drill_rig lvl1) boards the free drill_rig (vehicle #1). Without a driver the rig is a mesh and no drill_hole action ever starts.

Finding #46 (renumbered for staffed:true, unchanged reasoning): a backup surveyor, and in fact the ENTIRE hand-hired roster (all 8 hires below, now employees #6-#13), front-loaded here while cash is still healthy -- CrewPanel.ts's hire button disables on `state.cash < HIRING_COSTS[role]`, confirmed directly with a real click once cash is deep in the red from this file's own setup costs. A mid-game 'hire more staff' beat is not something a real player can click through once early spending has gone negative.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification; this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`. Employee ids renumbered +5 throughout for staffed:true's 5 free hires (was #1 pre-staffed).

Finding #47 (unchanged): the only warehouse type is `freight_warehouse` (Building.ts/balance.ts). Placed at (5,5), outside the blast footprint -- see Finding #47's original note for the full reasoning (a first attempt closer to the blast site got destroyed by a blast's clear radius).

#552/#553: staffed:true's free debris_hauler (vehicle #2) is reused here rather than buying a second one by hand -- the file's own hauling volume (one 260kg rubble delivery this cycle, matching Finding #48's fragment-matching constraint below) never needs a second hauler, and this file's budget cannot spare the $25,000 a manual purchase would cost on top of everything else -- see the file description's bankruptcy finding for just how tight that budget already is. Employee #10 (hired driver, licensed driving.truck lvl5 above) boards it. Re-opens the vehicles panel first (UIManager.togglePanel, same pattern as level2-playthrough-win's fix): the panel had switched to employees then build (the surveyor/driller/blaster/driver hires and the freight_warehouse placement above), so #bs-vehicle-panel's own [data-vehicle-id="2"] row was off-screen (display:none, zero size) at this point -- not a stale selector, the panel itself just wasn't the active one. togglePanel only closes an ALREADY-active panel, so this click safely switches to vehicles rather than toggling it shut. New finding, real interaction-mode CI: `.bs-vehicle-assign-btn` (`makeAssignRow`, fleetDetailSections.ts) reads a `<select>` next to it, not a fixed target -- clicking Assign without first choosing an option in that select just assigns whoever the browser's default selection lands on (its first eligible option), which for this vehicle is one of staffed:true's own free drivers (a lower employee id than the hired #10), not employee #10 named in the command. Confirmed directly: `vehicle list` after this step showed debris_hauler's `driver` as employee #3, not #10, and hauling still happened (#552 self-dispatch doesn't care WHICH qualified driver boards) but not the one this step names. Fixed with a `set` action on the row's own `select` (scoped by `[data-vehicle-id="2"]`, matching the file's other dropdown-driven steps) before the Assign click, mirroring the Charge step's own real-control convention (issue #515) rather than relying on whatever the dropdown defaulted to.

Finding #49 (unchanged): seismic ($3000) is unaffordable this late in setup; core_sample alone ($800) sends employee #6 (first hired surveyor) to survey (15,15), which the blast below then clears. #553/new: unlike the pre-#553 file, this survey now has time to actually finish -- ground rule #14's arrival-gating raced the surveyor against the blast, and pre-#553 the blast (an instant command) always won; now the driller needs 60 real ticks to land even a truncated pattern, so the survey completes long before the blast fires this time -- surveyCount below stays 0 only because 0 ticks have elapsed since this step, not because the result never arrives (see the closing surveyCount:1).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: Ground rule #15: depth corrected to 6, matching the grid-tool's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M. #553: confirming the grid only orders the 16 holes -- they are ghosts until the driller drives drill_rig #1 to each one, so holeCount is 0 here.

#553: sandbox-measured. The lone driller lands only 4 of the pattern's 16 holes in this window -- not the full drain the pattern set out to order. Landing all 16 (tutorial-playthrough.json's own solo-driller measurement: ~400 ticks for the same size pattern) would keep this file's cash below the $5,000 bankruptcy threshold for well over the 100-tick grace period (Bankruptcy.ts) -- see the file description's bankruptcy finding. This file blasts with the 4 that land instead of waiting for the rest, the only way any of drilling/blasting/hauling/contract-fulfillment survives to be exercised at all. Holes 5-16 never land: the pad stops here on purpose, not because 60 was too small a guess.

#554/new finding: charging is now real, queued work (one `charge_hole` action per hole, landed by a blaster physically walking to the hole) -- draining the charge queue below takes dozens of real ticks, during which drill_rig #1 (still holding 12 more ordered holes) keeps drilling regardless, landing 4 more holes inside that same window (confirmed directly: sandbox trace, holeCount 4->8 across the charge-wait alone). `sequence auto` sequences every currently-drilled hole unconditionally (autoVPattern over ctx.state.drillHoles, DrillPlan.ts) and `blast`'s own validateBlastPlan (BlastPlan.ts) requires a charge AND a sequence delay for every drilled hole with no partial-pattern option -- so any hole that lands after the charge order was placed can never be blasted without re-charging it, and re-charging costs further real ticks that let the driller land still more holes, a divergence that only resolves once the full 16-hole pattern is drilled (confirmed directly, sandbox trace across 3 recharge rounds: holeCount 4->8->12->15 and climbing), busting this file's own already-documented bankruptcy runway long before a second blast could ever happen. #553's own drilling-time budget and #554's own charging-time budget were each individually calibrated against an INSTANT partner action; wired together, the driller has nothing to stop it from outrunning the deliberately-truncated 4-hole pattern the instant charging needs its own real time too. Fixed the same way a player would: cancelling the 12 still-ordered (never-drilled) holes right after the tick-60 cutoff and before charging starts, via the Drill panel's own per-hole delete button (`drill_plan remove hole:<id>`, Drill.ts's `makeOrderedHoleRow` -- a real, player-clickable control, not a console-only shortcut). With nothing left ordered, the driller has no more work once its current in-flight hole (if any) finishes, so no ticks spent waiting on the charge queue ever grow holeCount past 4 again -- holeCount/chargedCount/sequencedCount converge cleanly at 4 instead of chasing a moving target. Ordered rows render before drilled rows in the panel (DrillStep.render, `...ordered.map(...), ...holes.map(...)`), so the SAME selector, clicked repeatedly, always removes the first remaining ORDERED hole -- never one of the 4 already-drilled ones -- letting this single selector serve for all 12 clicks. New finding: the driller (and any other blasting-qualified employee freed up once its own task ends) gets auto-dispatched to charge a hole in person and doesn't proactively leave once done -- so unlike the pre-#554 file (deathCount 1, only the surveyor near the survey tile), several of the employees who physically loaded a charge are still standing on their hole when it fires. See the blast step below for the resulting death toll, sandbox-confirmed and now hard-asserted for real.
Last of the 12 cancellations -- drill plan now holds exactly the 4 already-landed holes and nothing more, matching this file's original, deliberately-truncated pattern.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. `charge-all` only ever reaches the 4 already-drilled holes -- the 12 still-ordered ones are not chargeable yet, matching chargedCount below.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.
This value already matches the Sequence panel's own 25ms default (Sequence.ts DEFAULT_DELAY_STEP_MS) -- 0 stepper clicks needed, asserted rather than assumed (Finding #75).

Finding #46 (renumbered, same reasoning): employee #6 (the surveyor dispatched to survey (15,15)) is standing at/near that tile when this 4-hole blast clears it -- a real, reproducible casualty. Rated PERFECT with hundreds of fragments despite only 4 of 16 holes firing -- yield scales off charge density, not pattern completeness, sandbox-confirmed directly (302 fragments, 236 cleared voxels). Real root cause of the command-vs-interaction split previously documented here (deathCount 2 vs 1, vehicleCount 3 vs 4): the drill_plan step above was missing `diameter:` -- the same class of bug vibration-budget.json's own history already found and fixed (see that file's finances-step note) -- so command mode's `drill_hole` actions ran at mining.ts's console-only fallback diameter (0.15m) while interaction mode's real grid-tool click always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M (0.089m, Drill.ts); computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales duration by diameter, so the smaller real diameter drills measurably faster. With no diameter: specified, command mode's driller had less spare time left in this file's 60-tick drilling window and stayed idle at (22,15), parked among the holes it just drilled and inside this blast's radius. Fixed by adding diameter:0.089 to the drill_plan command, matching the real click exactly. `deathCount` updated for #554 (renumbered again): drill_rig #1 itself still survives (its driver, employee #1, was mid rest-cycle and dismounted onto the vehicle's own position at (15, 17.2666...) by #593's fix, then the 12 hole-cancellation steps above froze it there for good -- outside this blast's radius, matching `vehicleCount`:4 below) -- but charging is now real, in-person work (#554): every blasting-qualified employee the game auto-dispatched to load one of the 4 charges (employee #1 once its drilling task ended, staffed:true's own free blaster #2, and two of the hand-hired blasters/drillers) walked to that hole and stayed there once done, with the hired surveyor #6 from the original finding above. Five employees standing on live charges when they fire -- sandbox-confirmed directly (`employees.filter(e => !e.alive)`: #1 at H2's (18,15), #2 at H1's (15,15), #6 at (15,15), plus two more hired blasters at H2/H4) -- is the real, reproducible toll now, not an authoring gap.

wellBeing dropped from this equals block (issue #596's own rule): it settles wherever the charge-wait above (#554, real ticks now) happened to leave it, not a value this step's own read-only `scores` call moves or that the scenario's narrative depends on -- exactly the incidental-checkpoint case the rule calls out, so it is not re-captured as another precise float. safety/ecology/nuisance are still the file's own point here (unaffected by the blast at this exact instant, before any post-blast events fire) and stay hard-asserted.

#553/new: a `lucky_strike` event is already pending the instant this tick is requested (fired as a side effect of the blast above) -- 0 of the 10 requested ticks advance; the tick command itself refuses until the event is resolved, same as every other pending-event guard in this file. tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): its own point is that the pending event blocks the whole batch, not a specific running total -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. `lucky_strike`'s option 0 is a fixed $10,000 windfall ("A cash bonus goes straight to the company account for the unexpectedly rich yield") -- deterministic under this file's fixed seed, not the reason this file survives (still nowhere close to offsetting setup cost -- see the file description's bankruptcy finding).

Finding #48 (unchanged): the Fleet panel's Haul button always sends the vehicle to `findReachableGroundFragment` -- the NEAREST reachable, non-oversized fragment, with no regard for ore content -- and #552 self-dispatches hauling automatically, so a player cannot target a specific fragment by ore at all. The contract must match what the hauler will actually claim, not the reverse: this cycle's nearest reachable fragment carries no named ore, so the rubble-disposal contract (materialId '') is the one it can satisfy, confirmed by replaying this file's own exact command sequence. #554/new: contract id renumbered 2->4 -- the charge-wait above (real, queued `charge_hole` work, dozens of extra ticks) consumes a longer slice of the contract-generation RNG stream than the old instant-charge timing did, so by the time this step runs the generator has moved on to a later id for the same rubble-disposal contract type (`contract list` right before this step confirms it: `[4] Dispose of rubble`). Re-verified directly, not guessed -- an id shift here is exactly the kind of downstream consequence #554's own timing change forces. New finding, real interaction-mode CI: this step used to sit right after `contract list`, before the tick-10/event-choose pair above -- but `lucky_strike` (fired as a side effect of the blast, several steps up) is already pending by then, and unlike command mode, where a pending event is just state until something reads it, a real browser shows its modal (`.bs-confirm-overlay`) the instant it goes pending, sitting over the whole shell and blocking this step's own toolbar click (confirmed directly: `clickSelector` failed with "covered by div.bs-confirm-overlay"). Moved to after the tick-10/event-choose pair instead, which the file was already going to run anyway -- `lucky_strike` is resolved for real by the time this step's click reaches the toolbar, in both modes.
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered.
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to the charge-wait above (#554) landing on a different real-tick total.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

#552: hauling self-dispatched automatically once debris_hauler #2 (relocated close to the blast site, not off-map -- see the vehicle-move steps above) had somewhere to go; 30 ticks (the 3 tick-10 steps above) was enough for a full round trip and back, confirmed directly (storedMassKg > 260 by this point). One haul is enough to complete this 260kg contract outright, same as the pre-#552 flow's own single-haul sizing. Contract id renumbered 2->4 (see the `contract accept` step's own #554 finding); tickCount converted to `changedBy: 0` (issue #596) -- this step is itself a non-ticking console call, its own point is that delivery doesn't advance the clock, not a specific running total. deathCount updated 1->5, matching the blast step's own #554 finding (charging-in-person casualties).
tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning -- robust to upstream timing shifting the real-tick total this step starts from.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

Sandbox-confirmed: only 1 of the 10 requested ticks advances here -- a spontaneous event goes pending mid-batch (same `tick` guard as every other pending-event interruption in this file) after just 1 tick rather than after the full 10, unlike the other `tick 10` steps in this stretch. Left as `increased` rather than a pinned `changedBy` count -- the exact tick this particular event happens to interrupt on is incidental to what this step is testing (that the clock keeps moving at all), not the step's own subject.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

#553/new: the mine is seized by bankruptcy inside this window (ticksBelowThreshold reaches BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS=100 at cumulative tick 119, Bankruptcy.ts) -- cash has stayed under the $5,000 threshold continuously since shortly after setup, and the one contract delivery above was nowhere near enough to pull it back above that line. See the file description's bankruptcy finding for why no crew configuration sandbox-tested for this file avoids this. tickCount converted to `changedBy` (issue #596): a plain 10-tick advance, not a running total worth pinning.
Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons.

#596/#597: setupEvents idempotency + cooldown-threshold caching moved when `weather_geomagnetic_storm` goes pending -- this `tick 10` no longer gets interrupted partway (sandbox-measured, real run: full 116->126), unlike the pre-fix trajectory where only 9 of the 10 requested ticks advanced.
